title: PRD: Slice-driven safety, SLO-aware degradation and ops cutover for hosted endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Deliver a PRD and launch checklist for a new slice-driven safety and SLO-aware degradation framework applied to hosted API endpoints (completions/chat/embeddings/rerank). This work introduces endpoint slicing, automated degrade policies tied to observable SLOs, and an ops cutover checklist for safe canarying and rollback.
context_background: Customers run mixed workloads on hosted endpoints (low-latency chat, high-throughput embedding pipelines, and rerank pipelines). Incidents have shown that a single noisy workload or model regression can impact overall lane SLOs. We need a structured way to (1) define endpoint slices, (2) attach quality and latency SLOs per slice, (3) automate graded degradation policies (e.g., reduce batch sizes, route to smaller models, switch to cached responses), and (4) provide operators a safe cutover checklist for launch.
goals: Define slice taxonomy for hosted endpoints (by use-case, cost-sensitivity, determinism requirements)
Introduce SLO policy objects that can trigger automated, graded degradations per slice
Provide API/Console controls for slice assignment and traffic shaping
Deliver a robust launch checklist for canary, ramp, and rollback with telemetry and postmortem hooks
non_goals: Replacing existing tenant isolation or Dedicated offering
Full multi-cluster capacity rebalancing (out of scope for initial launch)
Extensive UI redesign — surface-level Console controls only
user_personas: Platform engineer at a SaaS company configuring latency-sensitive chat lanes
Growth product manager who needs a predictable embed pipeline for search
Redwood on-call engineer responsible for endpoint SLOs and runbook actions
product_requirements: Slice definition API: name, criteria (model tag, customer tier, route path), SLO targets (p50/p95 latency, availability, quality regression thresholds)
SLO policy engine that consumes telemetry, evaluates gates, and emits degradation actions
Degradation action set: model variant fallback, quantization-enabled variant, prefix cache reuse, batch-size cap, rate-limit soft quota
Console controls: create/edit slices, preview affected routes, enable automated actions, manual override/killswitch
Audit logs and traceability: every policy decision must log reason, triggering metric, and action taken
api_contract_changes: New POST /slices to create slice definitions with SLO targets
GET /slices/{id} and PATCH for policy toggles
Augment existing /endpoints listing with slice membership metadata
Events stream update for policy actions for downstream metrics consumers
acceptance_criteria: 1) Slice creation flow: user can create a slice via API or Console and assign existing hosted endpoints to it
2) Telemetry wiring: p50/p95 latency, 4xx/5xx, and quality eval signal (from eval harness) must be available to policy engine within 30s
3) Policy trigger: when p95 latency breaches the slice SLO for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows, the configured primary degrade action is executed automatically and recorded
4) Safety: automated degrade must include safe rollback (automatically revert if metrics improve within 10 minutes or on manual override)
5) Behavioral verification: quality regression (as measured by stored evals for a representative prompt set) is not worse than configured threshold after fallback to variant models
6) Cost guardrails: per-slice billing tags must continue to record token/embedding units accurately after routing changes
7) Observability: Console shows a slice timeline view with triggers, actions, and telemetry for the last 24h
8) Ops playbook: on-call can run the provided cutover checklist and roll back within the defined RTO (15 minutes)
launch_checklist: Draft PRD and circulate to eng/design/security — obtain written approvals
Implement and unit test SLO policy evaluation logic in staging
Integrate telemetry sources: runtime latency, request counters, eval quality webhook
Create sample slices for internal staging traffic (chat-fastlane, embed-bulk, rerank-low-latency)
Run chaos test: simulate noisy tenant and verify graceful degradation on other slices
Prepare Console UI toggles and audit log retention configuration
Create canary plan: 1% internal traffic -> 5% selected customers -> 25% broad beta -> 100%
Set feature flags and killswitch with immediate rollback capability
Document runbook and incident checklist; schedule on-call dry-run
Post-launch: run 72h validation with telemetry dashboard and automated regression checks
rollout_plan: Start with internal canary (1% of traffic) and two internal customers using different SLA profiles. Observe telemetry for 48 hours, then expand to 5% with a controlled set of customers. If no regressions and SLO stability holds, move to 25% beta for 7 days with continuous eval sampling. Final cutover to 100% only after monitored stability and sign-off from SRE, Product, and Security.
monitoring_and_slo: Latency SLOs: slice p50/p95 targets; alerts at 80%/90% of target
Availability SLO: successful-requests ratio per slice; paging if below threshold
Quality regression detection: periodic evals against canonical prompt sets; alert on >2% regression vs baseline
Policy action audit: count and duration of degrade actions per slice
telemetry_signals: eval.quality.score (batch from eval harness) and eval.regression_indicator
billing.token_units and embed_units with slice tag
qa_and_e2e_tests: Unit tests for policy evaluator with synthetic metric streams
Integration test: simulate latency regression and assert degrade action executed
E2E smoke: create slice via API, route a test request, and validate Console reflection
Regression harness: run representative prompts through primary and fallback models and assert quality thresholds
migration_and_customer_impact: Default behavior for existing endpoints is no-op; customers must opt into slices. For customers who map routes to slices, document behavioral changes (possible model fallbacks or cache reuse). Provide a migration guide for customers who require strict determinism. Customer-facing notices will be sent during beta ramp for impacted customers.
open_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives from noisy telemetry leading to unnecessary degrade -> Mitigation: require consecutive windows and allow manual override
Risk: model fallback causes quality drop for critical customers -> Mitigation: allow per-customer opt-out and preflight quality evaluation
Risk: billing attribution mismatches after routing changes -> Mitigation: end-to-end billing smoke tests and tagging enforcement in policy engine
Risk: operator overload from too many slice alerts -> Mitigation: aggregate alerts and implement runbook for triage
definition_of_done: Engineering implementation merged and deployed to staging
SLO policy engine validated against synthetic and production-like loads
Console slice UI shipped with audit logs visible
On-call runbook documented and at least one dry-run completed
Stakeholder sign-off: Product, SRE, Security, Developer Experience
